t.1.68.2: Today let all the treasurers, well prepared, go on ahead, taking abundant wealth and furnished with jewels of many kinds.
t.1.68.1: Then, when the night had passed, King Daśaratha, delighted, together with his preceptors and his kinsmen, spoke these words to Sumantra.
t.1.68.3: Let the fourfold army also set out swiftly in its entirety, and with it the finest carriages and draught animals, at the very moment of my command.
t.1.68.4: Vasiṣṭha and Vāmadeva, Jābāli and then Kāśyapa, the long-lived Mārkaṇḍeya, and likewise the sage Kātyāyana.
t.1.68.5: Let these twice-born go on ahead; have my chariot yoked, so that there may be no loss of time, for the messengers are urging me to hurry.
t.1.68.6: And at the command of the lord of men, that fourfold army followed behind the king as he went along with the sages.
t.1.68.8: Then King Janaka, delighted, approached the aged King Daśaratha, lord of men, and attained supreme joy; and that best of men spoke to the best of men, who was filled with gladness.
t.1.68.7: Having travelled the road for four days, he reached the land of the Videhas; and the glorious King Janaka, on hearing of it, arranged a ceremonial welcome.
t.1.68.9: Welcome to you, great king! By good fortune you have arrived, O Rāghava. You will obtain the joy of both your sons, won by their valour.
t.1.68.10: By good fortune the blessed sage Vasiṣṭha of great splendor has arrived, together with all the foremost of the twice-born, like Śatakratu with the gods.
t.1.68.11: By good fortune the obstacles have been overcome for me; by good fortune my family has been honored, through this alliance with the Rāghavas, great-souled and foremost in valor.
t.1.68.12: Tomorrow at daybreak, O lord among kings, at the close of the sacrifice, you should solemnize the marriage approved by the ṛṣis, O best of men.
t.1.68.13: Having heard those words of his, the lord of men, foremost among those skilled in speech, seated in the midst of the sages, replied to the king with these words.
t.1.68.14: Accepting a gift depends on the will of the giver; this I heard long ago. O knower of dharma, whatever you say, that we shall do.
t.1.68.15: Having heard those most righteous and glorious words of the speaker of truth, the lord of Videha was filled with the greatest astonishment.
t.1.68.16: Then all the hosts of sages, filled with great joy at their meeting with one another, spent that night happily.
t.1.68.18: Janaka too, of great splendor and knower of the truth, having duly performed according to dharma the rites of the sacrifice and those for his two daughters, spent the night there.
t.1.68.17: And the king, overjoyed at seeing his two sons, the Rāghavas, stayed there supremely pleased, well honored by Janaka.
